subject: How can I compute p-value of the competing models?

messages.author: 3440c66bcbf3c882
messages.subject: How can I compute p-value of the competing models?
parts:
Hi groups.
I have read through the posts and tried to run chisq as well as N.mixgof in order to find whether my models are fit the data. I don't know what I am doing wrong, but when I run the code (below) it takes half an hour to run and it returns all NA...

Please help me. I would like to know whether there is no evidence for lack of fit in my models.


#chisq code
chisq <- function(fm) {
  observed <- getY(umf)  ##umf is my data with covariates
  expected <- fitted(fm) ## fm is my model
  sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected) # Chisquared
}
pbfm<- parboot(fm, statistic = chisq, nsim = 1000, report=1)
pbfm
fm

pbfm16<- parboot(fm16, statistic = chisq, nsim = 1000, report=1)
pbfm16

Thanks.
Carole

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] How can I compute p-value of the competing models?
parts:
hi Carole,
 I'm going to guess that you have one or more missing values in your data set and, by convention, when you perform operations on objects containing missing values the result evaluates to a missing value.
 If I'm right about that, the easy fix is to add some code to the function like this:

 ...
  notna<- !is.na(observed)
 resid<- (observed-expected)^2/expected
 resid<- resid[notna]
 sum(resid)
}

perhaps this will work...
